data.title: Research: the landing page for kadence
body: # Research: the landing page for kadence
- **Question:** what the page that promotes kadence should look like, and which messages stand on it
- **Method:** a breakdown of the YC landing-page framework + a structural analysis of four real dev-tool pages + a check against the [positioning](DOC-29) and the [competitive snapshot](DOC-41)
- **Status:** decisions adopted 2026-09-03 — headline A (analytics), demo with `kadence ui`. Copy: [landing-copy.md](DOC-25)
## 1. What the YC framework says
Source: [Win the First 5 Seconds: The YC Landing Page](https://www.thevccorner.com/p/win-the-first-5-seconds-the-yc-landing).
The main claim: in five seconds a visitor decides "is this for me?". The median landing page converts at 6.6%, the top ones at 10–15%.
| Rule | Wording |
| Headline | *Outcome for [ICP] without [pain]* |
| Language | reading level ≤ grade 8; complex words take away ~24% of conversion |
| CTA | exactly one main one (attention ratio 1:1) |
| Demo | 10–60 s, shows the **result**, not the interface |
| Motion | static instead of carousels — "a carousel hides your strongest argument" |
| Speed | < 2 s to load |
| Proof | logos and named testimonials **above the fold**, not in the footer |
| Objections | a mini-FAQ next to the CTA, not a separate page |
The canonical section order: Hero → Problem/Transformation → How it works → Social proof → Pricing → Mini-FAQ → Footer.
## 2. Where this framework does not work for us

The framework is written for SaaS with a trial and pricing. kadence is an OSS CLI, and three of the seven sections are empty for us or mean something else. I looked at what real dev-tool landing pages do.
| Site | Headline | Main CTA | What it proves with |
| [biomejs.dev](https://biomejs.dev/) | "One toolchain for your web project" | Get started + View on GitHub | "~35x faster than Prettier" on a 171,127-line benchmark; 15 logos (AWS, Google, Vercel) |
| [bun.com](https://bun.com/) | "Bun is a fast JavaScript runtime & toolkit" | the install command itself in the hero | four benchmarks as bar charts; named quotes (Anthropic, Midjourney, Railway) |
| [zed.dev](https://zed.dev/) | "Your last next editor" | Download now + Clone source | three pillars (Fast/Agentic/Collaborative), a live commit feed as proof of activity |

| [Backlog.md](https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md) | "Markdown-native Task Manager & Kanban visualizer for any Git repository" | `npm i -g backlog.md` | a GIF of the board, 6.6k stars, conference talks; **no landing page of its own — the domain leads to GitHub** |
**Three findings that change the structure:**

1. **The CTA is the install command, not a button.** In Bun and Backlog.md the command stands in the first screen and is itself the conversion. A developer does not "subscribe" — he pastes a line into the terminal. One action, and the 1:1 attention ratio holds.

2. **The pricing section is replaced by a cost-of-ownership section.** In OSS you pay not with money but with weight: size, startup time, dependencies, licence, what happens on removal. This is exactly where our strongest numbers are — 32 KB, 80 ms, one dependency, MIT.

3. **Social proof in this category is not testimonials but measurements.** Biome leads with a benchmark, Bun with four benchmarks, Zed with a commit feed. Named quotes appear **after** the number has proved the claim. For us this is a gift: we have no users, but we do have measurements.
**The direct competitor has no landing page at all.** The domain `backlog.md` does a 301 to GitHub. Which means a well-made page is our advantage in the channel, not parity.
## 3. The uncomfortable truth: we have no social proof

The framework's most important section — "logos and testimonials above the fold" — is empty for us. Stars ~0, no users, no named quotes. We cannot put up "Trusted by developers worldwide": it is untrue, and the HN audience recognises that in seconds.
What we replace it with, in descending order of strength:
| Substitute | What exactly | From where |
| Measured proof of the claim | 8,396 merges across 130 repositories; task conflicts in 15% of repos; 89% of them are `content` | [probe-a-results.md](DOC-55) |
| Executable proof | an integration test: three people edit one task on three branches, merged in any order, zero conflicts | `test/integration/merge.test.ts` |
| Numbers that fall on a regression | 32 KB, 80 ms startup, 28 ms for 10,000 events | performance tests |
| Transparency | 390 tests, a CI badge, open ADRs with "what would make us reconsider" | `docs/decisions/` |
| Honest status | a separate block, "what is validated and what is not" | README |

The last item is counter-intuitive, but for this audience it is stronger than a testimonial. Not one of the four sites analysed writes what it has **not** proved. The block "Not validated: whether teams need velocity — the interviews have not been run yet" costs us part of the conversion and buys the trust everything else rests on. We put it low on the page, not in the hero: honesty is not a headline.
## 4. Recommended page structure
The order follows YC, with three sections replaced for OSS. The number is the content's load priority.
| # | Section | Content | Notes |

| 1 | **Hero** | H1 (outcome), subheading (ICP + without what), the install command with copy-to-clipboard, one "Quickstart" link under it, to the right/below — the output of `sprint close` as static text | the only main CTA. The terminal block is real text, not a picture: it copies, it indexes, it weighs nothing |

| 2 | **Micro-demo** | 40–50 s of asciinema: `init` → `task add` → **`kadence ui`, a task moving across the columns** → `sprint close`, which prints `1.6h per point` | the board inside the demo, the number in the last frame. No autoplay, one play on a click; the poster is the frame with the number |

| 3 | **Problem → Transformation** | Before: "every team estimates in points" → Agitate: "almost none can say what a point costs; the next sprint is planned on feel" → After: the number is derived from the journal the team already writes | we take the text from the positioning wording, we do not invent new ones |
| 4 | **Why events, not files** | state drifts · state conflicts · state forgets | the only place with cards. This is the main differentiation against Spec Kit, Beads and Backlog.md |

| 5 | **Proof of the claim about merging** | Probe A's numbers + links to the integration test and to the raw data | this is our "logo strip". We put it high precisely because it replaces social proof |
| 6 | **How it works** | three steps: `init` → the commands write events → `sprint close` counts. A diagram of `.kadence/` | secondary CTA — "Read the docs" |

| 7 | **Cost of ownership** (instead of Pricing) | a table: 32 KB · 80 ms · 1 dependency · MIT · offline. Risk reducers underneath | risk reducers in OSS terms: "Nothing leaves the machine", "Removal is `rm -rf .kadence`", "Your data is files anyone can read, including without us" |

| 8 | **For agents** | `board --json`, `schema: "kadence/v1"`, `KADENCE_SOURCE=agent`, the guide that `init` writes by itself | the best-proven need, but not a unique one — hence a section, not the headline |
| 9 | **Honest status** | what is validated / what is not / known limits | a separate block, visually calm, with no "but" |
| 10 | **Mini-FAQ** | 5 questions (below) | next to the repeated CTA, not as a separate page |
| 11 | **Footer** | GitHub, npm, docs, ADR, licence, changelog | |
What the page does **not** have: carousels, a popup, an email gate, a comparison with Jira and Linear, the word "tracker", logos of companies we do not have.
## 5. Copy for the hero — three options
The formula: *Outcome for [ICP] without [pain]*.
**A. Analytics (matches the current positioning — recommended)**
> **# Know what a story point actually costs your team.**
> kadence keeps tasks and sprints as plain files in your git repo, and derives velocity — and hours per point — from the journal your team already writes. No server, no account, no timesheets.
Outcome — "know what a point really costs". ICP — a team that keeps its tasks in the repo. Pain — "without timesheets". Reading level: grade 7.
**B. Git-native**
> **# Your sprint board lives in the commit.**
> Check out a release from three months ago and the tasks are exactly as they were that day.
A strong image, but it is proof, not a promise: the event is rare and goes unnoticed. We keep it as section 4, not as the headline.
**C. Agents**
> **# Task tracking your agents can read — no MCP server, no token, no network.**
The best-proven need, but here we are not unique: Backlog.md has MCP, git-issues has `.agent.md`. A candidate for a separate `/for-agents` page later, not for the home page.
**Adopted 2026-09-04 — the message is replaced.** The H1 is no longer about the cost of a point, but about shared context:
> **Your team and your agents, working from the same context.**

The reason is in the [positioning review](DOC-28): the "work in the repo" niche turned out to be taken, and what stayed uncovered was the loss of context between sessions. Options B and C below are kept as the history of the decision; velocity now lives in section 6 as a consequence of the journal. This is exactly what the positioning settled after Probe A — we do not change the decision at the layout stage.
**Main CTA:**
npm install -g kadence
A copy button, and under it on one line: `then kadence init` → a Quickstart link. The secondary "View on GitHub" goes in the navigation, visually quieter.
## 6. Mini-FAQ (the objections that will really arrive)
1. **Is this another tracker? We have Jira.** No. kadence does not replace Jira for the company — it gives the team a number that Jira does not have without manual entry. It lives alongside.
2. **What does it do to my repository?** It creates `.kadence/` and appends files there. It edits nothing, deletes nothing, and runs no git command on your behalf.
3. **Will outsiders see my tasks?** No. There is no network at all, no telemetry. This is checkable: turn off the internet.
4. **What happens if we change our minds?** `rm -rf .kadence`. The data is ordinary JSON files, readable without kadence.
5. **Why not GitHub Issues?** They do not follow the branch, they have no sprints and they do not count velocity. And they are not visible offline.
Format per the framework: one sentence + a link to the full answer.
## 7. The landing page as a probe

The positioning says it plainly: the bet on velocity is not validated, Probe B (the interviews) has not been run. The landing page is the cheapest way to get a first signal, and it is worth designing as a measurement, not only as a shop window.
**What we measure:**
| Signal | How | What it means |
| CTR on copying the install | an event on the button | the page's baseline conversion |
| Scroll depth to section 5 (proof) vs section 3 (the problem) | scroll markers | whether the "analytics" message holds |
| A click on "Read the docs" against a click on the "For agents" section | events | **the main one**: whether they go for velocity or for agents |
| Stars/issues after an arrival from HN | GitHub | traffic quality |

If traffic systematically escapes into the "For agents" section rather than into velocity, that is the same signal Probe B was meant to give, and the positioning has to be revised before writing the next materials.

**A tension that has to be named out loud:** the product is deliberately without telemetry, and the site has analytics. That is fine and these are different things, but the FAQ has to say it plainly: "The site counts anonymous page views. The CLI makes no network request at all".
## 8. Technical requirements
- Static, no framework. Budget: < 2 s on 3G, < 50 KB of critical path. Terminal blocks are text with CSS, not PNG.
- Font: a system stack + one monospace. No web fonts on the critical path.
- Theme: light and dark via `prefers-color-scheme`. The audience sits in dark.
- One H1. Title < 60 characters, meta < 155. Clean URLs: `/`, `/docs`, `/compare/backlog-md`.
- FAQ schema markup for snippets.
- Accessibility: 4.5:1 contrast in the terminal blocks (the most frequent mistake on dev landing pages — grey on near-black), visible focus, the demo does not autoplay.

- Hosting: **Vercel, our own domain** (adopted 2026-09-03). The page lives in the same repository, so the numbers in the table are taken from the same tests that fail on a regression. Turn Vercel Analytics off in favour of something that does not set cookies — otherwise we will have to ask for consent and put a banner on a page that promises "nothing leaves the machine".
## 9. Order of work
1. Write the copy in full (all 11 sections) — before layout, content-first.
2. Record the asciinema demo in which the last frame is `1.6h per point`.
3. Lay out the static page, measure the budget.
4. Put in the events from section 7.
5. Only after that — the channels: Show HN, Lobsters, r/devtools, the npm page, awesome-lists. The page has to be ready for the first wave, because there will be no second one from HN.
6. `/compare/backlog-md` — as a separate page after launch: bottom-funnel intent, and the direct competitor has no landing page at all.
## 10. Decisions adopted and what is left
| Question | Decision | Consequence |
| Headline | **Option A** — `Know what a story point actually costs your team` | B and C become sections 4 and 8. The message matches the positioning after Probe A |
| Demo | **We record it from `kadence ui`** | The board inside the demo, the last frame is `1.6h per point`. Section 4 gets a static frame of the board instead of a dynamic one |
| GitHub stars in the hero | Not until the number starts working for us | A badge that shows weakness is anti-proof |

**The risk in the demo decision, and how we remove it.** The README says it honestly: the TUI is verified by hand, only the key router (`src/tui/keys.ts`) is covered by unit tests. The demo will show the least verified part of the product, and four TUI bugs have already ridden past a green test suite once. So, before recording:
1. walk through the demo scenario by hand at least three times, at the same window size we record at;
2. keep in frame only what is in the scenario — movement between columns, the task detail, the exit. No editing fields, no mouse, no filter;
3. if something twitched in the recording — do not edit it out, fix it and re-record. An edited-out bug will arrive in an issue anyway;
4. re-record the demo after every change in `src/tui/` — the item is entered in the publication checklist.
**Left unresolved:**

- **Domain — resolved 2026-09-04:** `kadence.dev` is taken, as are the rest of the obvious options — the name belongs to the WordPress brand Kadence WP. We take `kadence.tools`. *Update 2026-09-13: `kadence.guru` has been bought and connected; `kadence.tools` was not bought.* The consequences for SEO are recorded in the [visual direction](DOC-18), section 11.
- **Who writes the English copy clean.** A draft of all eleven sections is done: [landing-copy.md](DOC-25). It needs proofreading by a native speaker, or at least a second pass on reading level.
